content.title: Health and Safety Plan – Summer Fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club

sections.heading: Hazard identification, assessment, control and review
sections.body: This is a public summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club at Hagley Park on 13 February 2027, from 11:00 to 18:00, with up to 350 people expected. The organiser will use a risk assessment form to identify, assess, control, and review hazards before and during the event. Hazards considered will include food stalls with on-site cooking, two marquees (each under 100 sqm), a fenced bar tent, inflatables, and amplified sound. Controls will be documented and reviewed throughout the event. The organiser will monitor for new hazards as the event progresses and update controls as needed.

sections.heading: Health and safety responsibilities
sections.body: Health and safety responsibilities will be assigned to named staff and volunteers. The event manager will oversee the health and safety system. Each area (food stalls, bar tent, inflatables, marquees) will have a designated supervisor responsible for hazard management in their area. List of responsible persons: Event manager: [EVENT MANAGER NAME]; Food area supervisor: [FOOD SUPERVISOR NAME]; Bar tent supervisor: [BAR SUPERVISOR NAME]; Inflatables supervisor: [INFLATABLES SUPERVISOR NAME]; Marquee supervisor: [MARQUEE SUPERVISOR NAME].

sections.heading: Staff competency and supervision
sections.body: All staff and volunteers will be assigned roles based on their experience and skills. Those without prior experience will be supervised by a competent person in their area. The organiser will ensure all staff and volunteers understand their tasks and are supervised as needed.

sections.heading: Pre-event site inspection
sections.body: The organiser will conduct a full site inspection of Hagley Park before the event opens. This will include checking the setup of marquees, bar tent fencing, food stalls, inflatables, and sound equipment for safety. Any hazards identified will be controlled or removed before the public is allowed on site.

sections.heading: Accident register
sections.body: An accident register will be kept at the event manager’s station on site. All incidents, injuries, and near misses will be recorded immediately.

sections.heading: Emergency plan
sections.body: The organiser will prepare an emergency plan for the event. This will cover fire, medical emergencies, severe weather, lost children, and evacuation procedures. Emergency exits will be marked on the site plan. Staff will be briefed on their roles in an emergency. Contact details for emergency services and key staff will be kept at the event manager’s station.

sections.heading: Health and safety briefings
sections.body: A documented health and safety briefing will be held for all staff and volunteers before the event opens and before each shift change. The briefing will cover hazard controls, emergency procedures, and reporting lines. Attendance will be recorded.

sections.heading: Working with partners and suppliers
sections.body: The organiser will meet with all partners and suppliers (food stall operators, bar staff, inflatables provider, marquee supplier) before the event to review health and safety arrangements. Each supplier will be required to follow the event’s health and safety plan and report any hazards or incidents to the event manager immediately.

content.title: Hazard Register – Summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club

sections.heading: Food Stall Operation and On-site Cooking
sections.body:
Activity: Preparing and serving food at four stalls, including on-site cooking.
Hazards: Burns, fire, hot surfaces, food contamination, slips from spills.
Persons at risk: Stall staff, volunteers, public (including children).
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: Cooking equipment will be set up on stable surfaces away from public access. Fire extinguishers and fire blankets will be provided at each stall. Staff will be briefed on safe food handling and emergency procedures. Spill kits will be available and spills cleaned immediately. Handwashing facilities will be provided for staff.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Monitor food stall areas throughout the event and review procedures after the event.
Owner: [FOOD STALL COORDINATOR NAME]

sections.heading: Alcohol Service in Fenced Bar Tent
sections.body:
Activity: Sale and service of alcohol in a fenced bar tent.
Hazards: Intoxication, disorderly behaviour, underage drinking, slips or falls.
Persons at risk: Bar staff, security, patrons, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: The bar area will be fenced and access controlled by security. Only persons with proof of age will be served. Staff will be trained in host responsibility and will monitor for intoxication. Water will be freely available. Security will be present at all times.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Review bar operations during and after the event.
Owner: [BAR MANAGER NAME]

sections.heading: Marquee Setup and Use (Two Marquees, Largest Under 100 sqm)
sections.body:
Activity: Erecting and using two marquees, largest under 100 sqm.
Hazards: Trips, falls, collapse in high winds, manual handling injuries.
Persons at risk: Setup crew, volunteers, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: Marquees will be installed by experienced crew following manufacturer instructions. Pegs and ropes will be clearly marked. Weather will be monitored and marquees evacuated if high winds are forecast. Only authorised staff will enter during setup and pack down.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Inspect marquees regularly during the event.
Owner: [SITE MANAGER NAME]

sections.heading: Inflatable Amusements
sections.body:
Activity: Use of inflatable amusements (e.g. bouncy castle).
Hazards: Falls, collisions, entrapment, deflation, wind-related movement.
Persons at risk: Children, supervising staff, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 4 = 16
Controls: Inflatables will be installed and supervised by trained operators. Maximum occupancy will be enforced. Inflatables will be anchored securely. Use will be suspended in high winds. Rules will be displayed and explained to users.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Ongoing supervision and weather monitoring.
Owner: [INFLATABLES SUPERVISOR NAME]

sections.heading: Amplified Sound
sections.body:
Activity: Use of amplified sound for announcements and music.
Hazards: Hearing damage, noise complaints, trip hazards from cables.
Persons at risk: Sound crew, performers, public (especially children).
Risk before control measures: Severity 3 x Likelihood 3 = 9
Controls: Speakers will be positioned away from direct public access. Volume will be kept at safe levels. Cables will be covered or routed away from walkways. Sound checks will be conducted before the event.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 1 x Likelihood 2 = 2
Additional controls: Monitor sound levels and cable safety during the event.
Owner: [SOUND TECHNICIAN NAME]

sections.heading: General Public Attendance (Including Children)
sections.body:
Activity: Large crowd movement and general attendance, including children.
Hazards: Lost children, slips, trips, crowding, minor injuries.
Persons at risk: All attendees, especially children and elderly.
Risk before control measures: Severity 3 x Likelihood 4 = 12
Controls: Clear signage and site maps will be provided. Lost child procedure will be in place and communicated to staff. First aid station will be clearly marked and staffed. Walkways will be kept clear. Staff and volunteers will be briefed on crowd management.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 1 x Likelihood 2 = 2
Additional controls: Review incident reports after the event.
Owner: [EVENT COORDINATOR NAME]

The application will be lodged no later than 4 December 2026, well before the 20 working day deadline and the summer non-working period. This is a one-off event.

sections.heading: Event details
sections.body:
Name of event: Summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club
Purpose: To raise funds for the Harewood Herons Netball Club through a community event with food, entertainment, and a licensed bar area.
This is a genuine one-off fundraising event, not a request for extra trading hours.
Areas to be licensed: Fenced bar tent (supervised designation – persons under 18 may be present only with a parent or legal guardian; no alcohol will be served to minors).
Entry arrangements: Open to the public, no tickets required. Access to the bar tent will be controlled by staff at entry points.
Entertainment and activities: Live amplified music, two marquees (each under 100m2), food stalls, and inflatables for children. No mechanical rides or stages over 1m high.
Expected attendance: 350 people, including families and children.

sections.heading: Conditions
sections.body:
Hours alcohol will be sold or supplied: 13 February 2027, 11:00 to 18:00.
Food: Four food stalls will operate, offering a range of hot and cold meals and snacks. Food will be provided by [FOOD STALL PROVIDERS].
Low-alcohol and non-alcoholic drinks: The bar will offer low-alcohol beer, soft drinks, juice, and water.
Drinking water: Free drinking water will be available at the bar tent and at each food stall.
Transport: The organiser will provide information on public transport options and local taxi services at the event entrance and bar area.
Prohibited persons: Bar staff will check identification and refuse service to minors, intoxicated persons, and anyone not attending the event. Security staff will monitor the bar area and entry points.
Staff, systems, and training: All bar staff will be briefed on responsible service of alcohol and procedures for checking ID and managing intoxication. The duty manager will supervise compliance.
Noise: Amplified sound will be managed by keeping speakers directed away from residential areas and monitoring volume throughout the event.
Disorder: Security staff will patrol the event area to prevent disorderly behaviour, nuisance, and vandalism. Any incidents will be reported to the duty manager and, if necessary, the police.

content.title: Alcohol Management Plan – Summer Fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club

sections.heading: Type of event
sections.body: The Summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club is a one-day, public, family-friendly event at Hagley Park on 13 February 2027, from 11:00 to 18:00, expecting up to 350 people. Alcohol will be sold from a fenced bar tent. The event includes food stalls, marquees under 100 sqm, and inflatables. The crowd will include adults and children. Risks include managing intoxication, underage drinking, and ensuring a safe environment for families. The event manager is [EVENT MANAGER NAME], with [BAR MANAGER NAME] responsible for the bar area, [SECURITY MANAGER NAME] for security, and [FOOD COORDINATOR NAME] for food stalls.

sections.heading: Promoting your event
sections.body: All pre-event communications, including social media and posters, will clearly state alcohol restrictions, age limits, and expected behaviour. Information about responsible drinking and the family-friendly nature of the event will be included in all promotions.

sections.heading: Intoxication
sections.body: Bar staff will monitor patrons for signs of intoxication and will refuse service to anyone showing signs. Staff will use a 'no service' protocol and notify security if intervention is needed. Any intoxicated person will be asked to leave the bar area and escorted to a safe place. Intoxicated patrons will be escorted to [SAFE PLACE LOCATION] where they can rest safely. The bar manager will oversee these procedures.

sections.heading: Food
sections.body: Four food stalls will operate throughout the event, with [FOOD COORDINATOR NAME] responsible for ensuring food is always available while alcohol is sold. If any food item runs out, it will be replaced with a similar item. Food options will be promoted with signage at the bar and throughout the event area.

sections.heading: Low and non-alcohol beverages
sections.body: A reasonable range of low and non-alcoholic beverages will be available at the bar at all times. The bar manager will ensure stock is maintained and options are promoted with signage and on the drinks menu.

sections.heading: Minors
sections.body: Anyone appearing under 25 will be required to show valid photo ID (passport, NZ driver licence, or Hospitality NZ 18+ card) before being served alcohol. Bar staff will be briefed on ID checking procedures. Procedures for minors accompanied by a parent or guardian will be confirmed: [CONFIRM: rule for minors accompanied by parent/guardian].

sections.heading: Signage
sections.body: The special licence and prohibited person signage will be displayed at each point of sale and at the entrance to the bar tent. [SIGNAGE RESPONSIBLE PERSON NAME] will ensure signage is visible and maintained throughout the event.

sections.heading: Safe transport
sections.body: Information about local taxi services, rideshare options, and public transport will be displayed at the exit and bar area. Staff will encourage patrons not to drive if they have been drinking and will offer to call a taxi if needed. A phone will be available at the bar for patrons to arrange transport.

sections.heading: Alcohol promotions on the day
sections.body: No promotions will encourage excessive drinking. There will be no discounts, drinking games, or alcohol as prizes. All promotions will focus on responsible enjoyment and will not target minors.

sections.heading: Staff training
sections.body: All staff, including bar, security, and volunteers, will be trained and briefed before the event. Training will cover host responsibility, licence conditions, intoxication monitoring, ID checks, and individual roles. The event manager will oversee the briefing and keep a record of attendees.

sections.heading: Incident and noting book
sections.body: An incident and noting book will be kept at the bar. All refusals of service, removals, incidents, and notable patron behaviour will be recorded by the bar manager or security. The event manager will review entries and act on any issues. Estimated attendance is 350.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: A certified security firm will be contracted. [SECURITY FIRM NAME] will provide [NUMBER OF SECURITY STAFF] security staff, present from 10:30 to 18:30. The security manager will liaise with the firm and oversee security operations. Security staff will be briefed before the event.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.body: The event will provide a relaxed, safe environment with appropriate lighting, seating, and family-friendly entertainment. Drinking games and activities promoting excessive consumption are not permitted. No alcohol or vouchers will be given as prizes. Adequate toilets will be available throughout the event area. Free water will be readily available and promoted throughout the event area. [WATER PROVISION RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will ensure water stations are stocked and signage encourages patrons to drink water.

sections.heading: Debriefing
sections.body: A debrief will be held with staff and contractors after the event to discuss any issues and identify improvements. The event manager will coordinate the debrief. Involvement of Police, Council, or Health will be considered if needed.

placeholders: [CONFIRM: rule for minors accompanied by parent/guardian]

items.text: Documents who is in charge of the event and each area of responsibility
items.evidence: The event manager is [EVENT MANAGER NAME], with [BAR MANAGER NAME] responsible for the bar area, [SECURITY MANAGER NAME] for security, and [FOOD COORDINATOR NAME] for food stalls.

items.text: Defines the type of event and its risks
items.evidence: The Summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club is a one-day, public, family-friendly event at Hagley Park on 13 February 2027, from 11:00 to 18:00, expecting up to 350 people. Alcohol will be sold from a fenced bar tent. The event includes food stalls, marquees under 100 sqm, and inflatables. The crowd will include adults and children. Risks include managing intoxication, underage drinking, and ensuring a safe environment for families.

items.text: Pre-event communication covers intoxication, alcohol restrictions, age limits and behaviour
items.evidence: All pre-event communications, including social media and posters, will clearly state alcohol restrictions, age limits, and expected behaviour. Information about responsible drinking and the family-friendly nature of the event will be included in all promotions.

items.text: Sets procedures to monitor patrons and prevent intoxication
items.evidence: Bar staff will monitor patrons for signs of intoxication and will refuse service to anyone showing signs. Staff will use a 'no service' protocol and notify security if intervention is needed. Any intoxicated person will be asked to leave the bar area and escorted to a safe place. Intoxicated patrons will be escorted to [SAFE PLACE LOCATION] where they can rest safely. The bar manager will oversee these procedures.

items.text: Identifies a safe place for intoxicated patrons
items.evidence: Intoxicated patrons will be escorted to [SAFE PLACE LOCATION] where they can rest safely.

items.text: Names who keeps food available while alcohol is sold
items.evidence: Four food stalls will operate throughout the event, with [FOOD COORDINATOR NAME] responsible for ensuring food is always available while alcohol is sold.

items.text: Keeps a reasonable range of low and non-alcohol drinks available at all times
items.evidence: A reasonable range of low and non-alcoholic beverages will be available at the bar at all times. The bar manager will ensure stock is maintained and options are promoted with signage and on the drinks menu.

items.text: Free water is readily available and promoted
items.evidence: Free water will be readily available and promoted throughout the event area. [WATER PROVISION RESPONSIBLE PERSON] will ensure water stations are stocked and signage encourages patrons to drink water.

items.text: Sets ID checks for anyone appearing under 25
items.evidence: Anyone appearing under 25 will be required to show valid photo ID (passport, NZ driver licence, or Hospitality NZ 18+ card) before being served alcohol. Bar staff will be briefed on ID checking procedures.

items.text: Licence displayed and prohibited-person signage at each point of sale
items.evidence: The special licence and prohibited person signage will be displayed at each point of sale and at the entrance to the bar tent. [SIGNAGE RESPONSIBLE PERSON NAME] will ensure signage is visible and maintained throughout the event.

items.text: Lists safe transport options and how they are promoted
items.evidence: Information about local taxi services, rideshare options, and public transport will be displayed at the exit and bar area. Staff will encourage patrons not to drive if they have been drinking and will offer to call a taxi if needed. A phone will be available at the bar for patrons to arrange transport.

items.text: Promotions do not encourage excessive drinking
items.evidence: No promotions will encourage excessive drinking. There will be no discounts, drinking games, or alcohol as prizes. All promotions will focus on responsible enjoyment and will not target minors.

items.text: All staff are trained and briefed before the event
items.evidence: All staff, including bar, security, and volunteers, will be trained and briefed before the event. Training will cover host responsibility, licence conditions, intoxication monitoring, ID checks, and individual roles. The event manager will oversee the briefing and keep a record of attendees.

items.text: Keeps an incident and noting book
items.evidence: An incident and noting book will be kept at the bar. All refusals of service, removals, incidents, and notable patron behaviour will be recorded by the bar manager or security. The event manager will review entries and act on any issues.

items.text: Details certified security (guideline: over 100 patrons)
items.evidence: A certified security firm will be contracted. [SECURITY FIRM NAME] will provide [NUMBER OF SECURITY STAFF] security staff, present from 10:30 to 18:30. The security manager will liaise with the firm and oversee security operations. Security staff will be briefed before the event.

items.text: Adequate toilets throughout the event
items.evidence: Adequate toilets will be available throughout the event area.

content.title: Hazard Register – Summer fundraiser for the Harewood Herons Netball Club

sections.heading: Food Stall Operation and On-site Cooking
sections.body:
Activity: Preparing and serving food at four stalls, including on-site cooking.
Hazards: Burns, fire, hot surfaces, food contamination, slips from spills.
Persons at risk: Stall staff, volunteers, public (including children).
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: Cooking equipment will be set up on stable surfaces away from public access. Fire extinguishers and fire blankets will be provided at each stall. Staff will be briefed on safe food handling and emergency procedures. Spill kits will be available and spills cleaned immediately. Handwashing facilities will be provided for staff.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Monitor food stall areas throughout the event and review procedures after the event.
Owner: [FOOD STALL COORDINATOR NAME]

sections.heading: Alcohol Service in Fenced Bar Tent
sections.body:
Activity: Sale and service of alcohol in a fenced bar tent.
Hazards: Intoxication, disorderly behaviour, underage drinking, slips or falls.
Persons at risk: Bar staff, security, patrons, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: The bar area will be fenced and access controlled by security. Only persons with proof of age will be served. Staff will be trained in host responsibility and will monitor for intoxication. Water will be freely available. Security will be present at all times.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Review bar operations during and after the event.
Owner: [BAR MANAGER NAME]

sections.heading: Marquee Setup and Use (Two Marquees, Largest Under 100 sqm)
sections.body:
Activity: Erecting and using two marquees, largest under 100 sqm.
Hazards: Trips, falls, collapse in high winds, manual handling injuries.
Persons at risk: Setup crew, volunteers, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 3 = 12
Controls: Marquees will be installed by experienced crew following manufacturer instructions. Pegs and ropes will be clearly marked. Weather will be monitored and marquees evacuated if high winds are forecast. Only authorised staff will enter during setup and pack down.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Inspect marquees regularly during the event.
Owner: [SITE MANAGER NAME]

sections.heading: Inflatable Amusements
sections.body:
Activity: Use of inflatable amusements (e.g. bouncy castle).
Hazards: Falls, collisions, entrapment, deflation, wind-related movement.
Persons at risk: Children, supervising staff, public.
Risk before control measures: Severity 4 x Likelihood 4 = 16
Controls: Inflatables will be installed and supervised by trained operators. Maximum occupancy will be enforced. Inflatables will be anchored securely. Use will be suspended in high winds. Rules will be displayed and explained to users.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 2 x Likelihood 2 = 4
Additional controls: Ongoing supervision and weather monitoring.
Owner: [INFLATABLES SUPERVISOR NAME]

sections.heading: Amplified Sound
sections.body:
Activity: Use of amplified sound for announcements and music.
Hazards: Hearing damage, noise complaints, trip hazards from cables.
Persons at risk: Sound crew, performers, public (especially children).
Risk before control measures: Severity 3 x Likelihood 3 = 9
Controls: Speakers will be positioned away from direct public access. Volume will be kept at safe levels. Cables will be covered or routed away from walkways. Sound checks will be conducted before the event.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 1 x Likelihood 2 = 2
Additional controls: Monitor sound levels and cable safety during the event.
Owner: [SOUND TECHNICIAN NAME]

sections.heading: General Public Attendance (Including Children)
sections.body:
Activity: Large crowd movement and general attendance, including children.
Hazards: Lost children, slips, trips, crowding, minor injuries.
Persons at risk: All attendees, especially children and elderly.
Risk before control measures: Severity 3 x Likelihood 4 = 12
Controls: Clear signage and site maps will be provided. Lost child procedure will be in place and communicated to staff. First aid station will be clearly marked and staffed. Walkways will be kept clear. Staff and volunteers will be briefed on crowd management.
Residual risk after control measures: Severity 1 x Likelihood 2 = 2
Additional controls: Review incident reports after the event.
Owner: [EVENT COORDINATOR NAME]

The hazard register will be distributed to all persons named as owners: [FOOD STALL COORDINATOR NAME], [BAR MANAGER NAME], [SITE MANAGER NAME], [INFLATABLES SUPERVISOR NAME], [SOUND TECHNICIAN NAME], and [EVENT COORDINATOR NAME].
